name: ANSI/IEEE permanent-magnet synchronous generator symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented library form of a three-phase synchronous generator with permanent-magnet excitation, with reading notes.
description: This entry covers the permanent-magnet synchronous generator as it appears in an IEEE-oriented drawing library. The machine has a magnet rotor and no field winding, so output voltage rises with speed and cannot be trimmed by an excitation regulator; voltage control is done by the converter or by the load.

Within IEEE-style one-line and schematic drawings the machine is a circle with the generator letter and a magnet indication, with three output leads. The block identifier quoted here is a vendor library name and only meaningful inside that library. This is a convention-specific lookup; the geometry is independently drawn and is not a certified reproduction of the standard graphic.
readingNotes: Expect a converter or rectifier immediately downstream; a permanent-magnet machine rarely connects directly to a fixed-frequency bus.
Read the vendor block name only within the library it belongs to.
drawingChecklist: State rated speed and voltage at that speed.
Show the converter or rectifier interface.
Cross-reference the counterpart IEC-style entry where both conventions are used.
distinction: A permanent-magnet generator has no field winding to regulate; a wound-field synchronous generator has an exciter and regulator.
